title: The Hatch That Could Not Be Opened From Inside

scenes.voiceover: Three astronauts died because their own capsule's hatch could not be opened from the inside. Not during a launch. During a rehearsal.
scenes.mainText: A HATCH THAT COULD NOT BE OPENED FROM INSIDE

scenes.voiceover: January 27th, 1967. Grissom, White and Chaffee are sealed inside their capsule, running a routine countdown test. The rocket beneath them isn't even fueled.
scenes.mainText: A ROUTINE TEST. AN UNFUELED ROCKET.

scenes.voiceover: The cabin is pressurized with almost pure oxygen. A spark starts a fire, and in that atmosphere, it spreads almost instantly.
scenes.mainText: PURE OXYGEN. A SPARK. INSTANT FIRE.

scenes.voiceover: The hatch opens inward, held shut by internal pressure. Once the fire raised that pressure, no one alive could pull it open. The pad crew took over five minutes to get it off.
scenes.mainText: OVER 5 MINUTES TO OPEN IT. TOO LATE.

scenes.voiceover: The design was changed forever. Every hatch on every capsule since opens outward, fast, in seconds. Grissom and Chaffee rest at Arlington. White, at West Point, by his own wish.
scenes.mainText: EVERY HATCH SINCE OPENS OUTWARD. IN SECONDS.

scenes.voiceover: They were the first of 18 people who've died flying toward space. What happened to every one of them is on the channel.
scenes.mainText: 18 PEOPLE. THE FULL STORY → ON THE CHANNEL
